global_style: You are narrating a bedtime picture book for a 3 to 5 year old Arabic-speaking child. Read in Modern Standard Arabic with a calm, warm, low voice, as if sitting beside the child in a dimly lit room. Keep loudness constant and identical across every line. Never sound tense, worried, excited or surprised. No gasps, no exclamations, no dramatic build-up.

lines.style: Steady and welcoming. Pronounce the name زُغب clearly with a short u vowel on the first letter; this is the first time the child hears it.
Gentle and matter-of-fact. No anticipation, no excitement.

lines.text: طار إلى الشجرة. ثم أبعد قليلًا.
lines.style: Even pace with a small natural pause between the two sentences. Do not let the pitch rise on أبعد.
This is the story's peak and it must stay completely calm. Give خفيفة its shadda clearly but with zero tension. Absolutely no volume increase, no urgency, no drama.

lines.text: نظر زُغب إلى بيته. وعرف طريقه.
lines.style: Quiet confidence on وعرف طريقه. He is sure, not relieved and not searching.
Warmth on تنتظره, soft and affectionate, still at the same loudness.
Slow down on والريح هدأت and let it settle. Softer, sleepier, but not quieter in level.
Slowest line of the story, about 75 words per minute. Begin after a short silent beat. Read it as a closing statement of stillness, not a goodbye and not a question.
